items.name: Cathedral Rock
items.body: Sedona's most photographed formation. The actual summit trail requires hand-over-hand rock scrambling — not a fit for a relaxed pace or a first solo trip. The pathway and vista viewpoints deliver the same red-rock views without the climb. Considered sacred by the Yavapai and Hopi; stay on trail, keep voices low.

items.name: Bell Rock
items.body: A mostly flat pathway with constant red-rock views and none of Cathedral Rock's scramble — the better pick for an easy morning. Requires the Red Rock Pass for trailhead parking.

items.name: Tlaquepaque Arts & Shopping Village
items.kicker: Spanish colonial courtyards, not a mall
items.body: Built around existing sycamore trees rather than clearing them — galleries, boutiques, and restaurants inside genuinely distinctive architecture. Fri–Sun keeps later hours (10am–6pm) than the Mon–Thu schedule (10am–5pm).

img.alt: Tlaquepaque Arts & Shopping Village courtyard in Sedona

items.name: Airport Mesa Viewpoint
items.kicker: Free sunset views, if you're early
items.body: 360-degree red-rock views from a rim pulled right off Airport Road. The rim pullouts are free but hold only a few cars each — arrive 30-45 minutes before sunset. A paid upper lot (⚠ ≈$3 — confirm current rate) is the fallback if the free spots are gone.

img.alt: Sunset view from Airport Mesa near Sedona

items.name: Chapel of the Holy Cross
items.kicker: Free, quiet, and open every day
items.body: A modernist chapel built directly into the red rock in 1956, its cross-shaped facade rising above the valley south of town. Free to enter, no reservation needed — open daily 9am–5pm (last entry 4:45pm); the small gift shop keeps slightly shorter hours. South of Sedona proper, well outside the Oak Creek Canyon fire-closure area, so it works as a calm any-time-of-day stop rather than a sunset-only one.

items.name: Red Rock State Park
items.kicker: A creekside nature preserve, not another formation to climb
items.body: A 286-acre preserve along Oak Creek, ≈10 miles southwest of the "Y" — trails loop along the water and up to the House of Apache Fire overlook. A slower, greener counterpoint to the bare-rock stops closer to town, and a genuinely different kind of morning. Open daily 8am–5pm (later in summer); ⚠ ≈$10/adult entrance fee — confirm current rate. It's a state park, not national forest, so the Red Rock Pass doesn't cover it.

items.name: Slide Rock State Park
items.kicker: The swim spot — check the closure first
items.body: A natural sandstone water slide into Oak Creek, plus a preserved 1910s apple-orchard homestead. ⚠ The Oak Creek swim area itself is closed following Pocket Fire ash and flood debris — sources disagree on the exact reopening date (some cite through Sep 30, one cites early August), so treat swimming as unconfirmed for this trip's dates rather than assuming it's back. The park itself remains open for hiking, picnicking, and the Clifftop Nature Trail regardless. Open daily 8am–5pm; ⚠ ≈$30/car entrance fee (May–Sep rate) — confirm current rate before you go.

items.name: Sedona Heritage Museum
items.kicker: Ranching and film history in one short stop
items.body: Housed in the Jordan family's original homestead in Jordan Historical Park, Uptown — orchard equipment and Sedona's decades as a Western-movie filming location, told in a compact, unhurried space. Open daily 11am–3pm; ⚠ ≈$10 adult admission (children under 13 free) — confirm current rate.

items.name: Amitabha Stupa & Peace Park
items.kicker: Free hilltop quiet, no photo-op crowd
items.body: Two Buddhist stupas, a Shakyamuni Buddha statue, and a Native American medicine wheel on a red-rock ridge in west Sedona — a short uphill walk to a genuinely quiet spot rather than a staged one. Free to visit; ⚠ on-site parking hours vary by season (≈8:30am–5:30/6pm) — confirm before a very early or late visit.

items.name: Red Rock Crossing / Crescent Moon Picnic Site
items.kicker: The classic Cathedral Rock reflection shot
items.body: Cathedral Rock mirrored in Oak Creek, from a Forest Service picnic site ≈7 miles southwest of town — a calmer, different vantage than hiking the formation itself. South of the fire-closure area, unaffected by it. Open 7am–7pm through September; requires the Red Rock Pass or a separate day-use fee (⚠ ≈$15/vehicle — confirm current rate).
